text:
jordan: noticing weird provisioning latency in ap-southeast-1 — cluster-autoscaler keeps adding spot nodes that terminate almost immediately, pending pods piling up. @meenal @bryce can you take a look?

infra-bot: ALERT: spot-interruptions detected in ap-southeast-1 for fleet gpu-spot-1 — 18 termination notices in 5m. Recommended: failover to reserved pool if >10 interrupts.

meenal: ack. looking now. saw NodeGroup gpu-spot-1 scale 12 -> 26 -> 9 in ~7m :grimacing: lots of churn.

bryce: sounds like CA cooldown/backoff + underlying spot termination wave. also some pods have PDBs blocking drains which prevents clean eviction.

jordan: inference-prod tail latencies spiking, a bunch of pods are Pending with Insufficient resources (gpu/memory). cost is also spiking from repeat provisioning.

rita: can we flip traffic to reserved fallback? reserved-gpu-eu has idle capacity that could take batch + non-latency critical pods.

meenal: plan: disable aggressive scale-down for the spot group and taint it for new scheduling while we migrate non-critical pods. trying an emergency annotation.

bryce: proposed quick mitigations:
- annotate nodegroup to disable scale-down
- cordon noisy instances
- taint spot nodes so new pods avoid them
- migrate low-priority jobs to reserved pool

jordan: annotation command:
```kubectl annotate nodegroup gpu-spot-1 infra.redwood/scale-down-disabled=true --overwrite
```

infra-bot: RUNBOOK: when spot churn >10% in 10m -> recommend failover to reserved pool, disable CA scale-down on affected nodegroup, and set alert for eni/az exhaustion.

ally-oncall: cordoning noisy nodes and starting drains now. migrating low-priority batch pods with eviction-priority.

rita: taint + cordon applied. started evictions; about 60 batch pods in migration. CA still attempting to provision more spots though.

meenal: CA logs show AddNode -> NodeReady -> TerminationNotice within ~90s repeatedly. Looks like partial provisioning due to per-AZ soft limits (ENI quota) so some instances never complete networking attach. That triggers CA reattempts and a loop.

bryce: good call. check ENI quotas per AZ — we've hit ENI limit in az-a which causes attach failures and leaves instances in NotReady / NotAttached state.

jordan: kubectl get events shows the error:
```Warning FailedCreate pod/web-1 failed to create pod: failed to attach network interface: eni quota exceeded
```

ally-oncall: opened quota requests with our provider for az-a. meanwhile I'm spinning up reserved fallback in us-east and increasing warm pool in reserved-gpu-eu to absorb migrated jobs.

rita: cost note: keeping reserved fallback for ~2h estimated additional spend ~ $1.8k but prevents SLA impact. documenting in the incident channel.

meenal: applied CA config changes: set --scale-down-unneeded-time=30m (from 10m), --expander=priority, and temporarily disabled autoscaling for gpu-spot-1 nodegroup. confirmed config rolled out.

jordan: tail latencies are stabilizing and pending count is dropping. can we capture action items for a short postmortem?

bryce: suggested followups:
1) ENI quota increase and audit per-AZ quotas
2) adjust CA defaults for spot-heavy fleets (cooldowns, expander)
3) enforce eviction policies and prioritize batch workload scheduling
4) implement automatic fallback routing to reserved pools on spot-interrupt spikes
5) add metric/alert for spot-termination-rate >5/min

ally-oncall: logs, CA traces, and kube events archived to s3://rwd-infra/incidents/1985129999 for postmortem and runbook updates.

jordan: thanks all — will schedule a 20m tuning session to bake these changes into defaults. :thumbsup:
